changelog: Added a core principle that forbids avoiding contradiction risk by moving cuts onto function-word boundaries and instructs keeping short function words attached to content words — to address the primary finding that scorers dodge high-contradiction positions by splitting determiners/auxiliaries/list items, which reduces cohesion.
Replace C3 to emphasize preserving predicate-argument and noun-phrase integrity (addresses finding 2).
Insert a new core-principle after C4 that forbids dodging contradiction by moving cuts onto function words; instruct keeping function words attached to content (addresses finding 1).

Delete examples E3, E4, E5, E7, E8, E9, E10, E11, E13, E14, E15, E16 to meet the size budget and keep a small representative set of examples that illustrate the prioritized principles (per the critique's guidance to prefer compact, focused examples).
Replace E1 with measured example en_us_399 to show scorers the harm of moving cuts onto function-word boundaries and how that reduces cohesion (addresses primary finding).
Replace E2 with measured example en_us_845 to illustrate function-word splitting in lists/phrases and its cohesion cost (addresses primary finding).
Replace E3 with measured example en_us_345 to teach preserving enumerations and keeping short function words attached to content words (addresses primary finding).
Replace E4 with measured example en_us_1253 to show the cost of cutting inside noun/verb argument spans (supports the secondary finding about predicate-argument and NP integrity).

Replace C2 to explicitly require preserving predicate-argument and noun-phrase integrity (keeps verbs with auxiliaries/objects and determiners with nouns) to address the primary finding that cuts often split verb+object or determiner+noun and harm cohesion.
